instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Press a single dumbbell flat between your palms and hold it just above your chest, elbows close to your torso.
3. Push the dumbbell upward by extending your arms, squeezing your palms together throughout.
4. Fully extend your arms at the top while keeping the squeeze on the dumbbell.
5. Lower the dumbbell back to your chest with control, maintaining the squeeze. Repeat.
tips:
1. Squeeze the dumbbell hard the whole set to keep tension on the chest.
2. Exhale as you press up and inhale as you lower.
3. Keep your elbows tracking close to your body.
4. Start light to groove the palm squeeze before adding load.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with arms extended straight up, palms facing each other.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells behind your head with control.
4. Stop when your forearms reach roughly parallel to the floor.
5. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbells back to the top, keeping your upper arms still. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed so only the forearms move.
2. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo to keep tension on the triceps.
4. Let the dumbbells stretch the triceps behind the head for full range.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at chest level, arms slightly bent, palms facing up.
3. Raise the dumbbells over your chest in a wide arc, rotating your palms to face backward as you lift.
4. Pause briefly at the top with the dumbbells over your chest.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down in a wide arc, rotating your palms to face up again. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
2. Drive the movement from the chest, not the shoulders.
3. Control the lowering phase to keep tension on the upper chest.
4. Stop short of letting the dumbbells touch at the top.

instructions:
1. Set an incline bench to 45 degrees and lie back against it.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, gripping the handle, arms extended straight above your shoulders.
3. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head with control.
4. Stop when your forearms reach roughly parallel to the floor and feel the triceps stretch.
5. Extend your elbows to press the dumbbell back to the top, keeping your upper arms still. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your upper arms fixed so only the forearms move.
2. Exhale as you extend and inhale as you lower.
3. Use a slow, controlled tempo to protect the elbows.
4. Grip the dumbbell securely with both hands to keep it stable.

instructions:
1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand, arms in front of your chest with palms facing each other.
2. Keep your back straight and squat down, lowering your hips.
3. Drive up to stand while opening your arms out to the sides to shoulder level, forming a T.
4. Pause at the top with arms parallel to the floor, palms facing forward.
5. Bring your arms back in front of your chest as you squat down again. Repeat.
tips:
1. Move slowly and avoid using momentum to swing the dumbbells.
2. Keep your wrists straight and in line with your forearms.
3. Brace your core to stay balanced through the squat and raise.
4. Start light to coordinate the squat and lateral raise.
